title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors after harassing a former mistress and misusing police databases. After she ended the relationship in April 2024, he sent her thousands of texts, calls, and social media messages over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in a day. He also called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in one day. Between June and December 2023, he made 13 unauthorized searches in a state law enforcement database on his mistress, someone she dated, and his wife. He also used a police license plate reader system to track vehicles, even after being placed on leave.

On June 28, 2024, he was served with an emergency protective order and told he would be fired. He then drove by the woman's home, violating the order, and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, after already spending nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review is still pending.
